description.cancellation_policy:
Reservation changes and cancellations more than one week before entry date:

  • Cancellations are refunded the $5 per person recreation fee.
  • Changes to exit location and date and nightly itinerary allowed.
  • Changes to party size are allowed subject to availability. Increasing party size will incur an additional $5 per person recreation fee. Decreasing the party size will refund a $5 per person recreation fee.

Reservation changes and cancellations one week or less before the entry date:

  • Cancellations are not refunded fees.
  • Party size can be decreased but no fees will be refunded.

At the issuing station:

  • Changes to exit location and date, and nightly itinerary can made when the permit is issued. 
  • If quota is available, increases in party size and changes to entry location and date may be made; these will incur additional fees.
description.comment_box_description: Please use comment box to request an alternate parking area. Requests are not guaranteed and are based on availability. Requests must be made at least 7 days before the start of your trip. Your final parking location will be viewable on your printed permit.
description.description:
Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks protect one of America's most diverse, rugged, and scenic landscapes. In September of 1964, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Wilderness Act , which made the preservation and protection of such wild places a national priority. As a result of that act and subsequent legislation, Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks currently protect more than 1,300 square miles of designated and recommended wilderness, or approximately 97% of the parks.

The parks overlie an extraordinary continuum of ecosystems arrayed along the greatest vertical relief (1,370 to 14,505 feet in elevation) of any protected area in the lower 48 states. Magnificent glacial canyons, broad lake basins, lush meadows, and sheer granite peaks--hallmarks of the most rugged portion of the High Sierra--form the core of the largest expanse of contiguous wilderness in California. These are the ancestral lands of the Mono/Monache, Paiute, Tübatulabal, and Yokuts; a unique place valued and visited by people from around the world.

Well-known destinations such as Mount Whitney and popular itineraries such as the John Muir Trail, Pacific Crest Trail, High Sierra Trail, and Rae Lakes Loop are heavily traveled and there is high demand for limited entry. The relatively accessible lake basins near Lodgepole and Mineral King are busy on weekends but can be quiet mid-week. Lesser-known destinations such as the Monarch Divide, Roaring River country, eastern slopes of the Great Western Divide, and the Hockett Plateau can offer outstanding opportunities for solitude throughout the year.

The popularity of these mountains mean that every visitor must minimize their impacts to the land and its community of life. Small actions repeated thousands of times have the potential to degrade the wilderness for current and future generations. Take the time to learn how you can protect this place by reading and understanding the requirements to minimize your impacts while visiting.
description.discounts:
There are no discounts for wilderness permits and reservations.

Guests of the Bearpaw High Sierra Camp are exempt from permit fees unless remaining overnight elsewhere in wilderness.

Reduced or waived entry fees are available for some groups and on some dates.
description.driving_directions:
To Grant Grove (Kings Canyon National Park) From Fresno

  • Permits issued at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center
  • Distance: 60 mi / 97 km
  • Time: 1 hour 15 minutes
  • Follow CA-180 E to the Big Stump entrance station and continue 3 mi. to the Grant Grove Village.

To Cedar Grove (Kings Canyon National Park) From Fresno

  • Permits issued at the Roads End Permit Station
  • Distance: 90 mi / 145 km
  • Time: 2 hours 15 minutes
  • Follow CA-180 E to the Big Stump entrance station, continue 37 mi. through Grant Grove Village to the road's end.

To Ash Mountain (Sequoia National Park) From Visalia

  • Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office
  • Distance: 40 mi / 64 km
  • Time: 50 minutes
  • Follow CA-198 E to the Ash Mountain entrance station and continue 1 mi. to the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.
  • Shuttle service may be available.

To Lodgepole (Sequoia National Park) From Visalia

  • Permits issued at the Lodgepole Visitor Center
  • Distance: 60 mi / 96km
  • Time: 1 hour 45 minutes
  • Follow CA-198 E to the Ash Mountain entrance station and continue 16 mi. to Giant Forest.
  • Shuttle service may be available.
  • Vehicles over 22 ft. length not advised - in summer, approach via Grant Grove and Generals Hwy.

To Mineral King (Sequoia National Park) From Visalia

  • Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station
  • Distance: 62 mi / 100 km
  • Time: 2 hours 30 minutes
  • Follow CA-198 E to Three Rivers, then follow the Mineral King Road for 25 mi. 
  • The Mineral King Road is narrow, steep, rough, and undivided. Caution is advised.
description.fee_policy:
• Permit Reservation Fee: $15 non-refundable for each wilderness permit during quota season.*
  • Per person fee: a $5 per person refundable fee is required for each wilderness permit during quota season.

The park will issue the permit only to the group or alternate leader identified at the time of reservation. Reservations and permits are not transferable. Photo identification required. 

*Note: Fees for reservations or walk-up permits are the same. 80% of fees directly fund projects in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks that improve visitor experience including road and trail maintenance, signage, and visitor information. 

  • Entrance Fee: The park charges an entrance fee which you may pay upon arrival or purchase in advance. The park honors valid annual or lifetime America the Beautiful-the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Passes (e.g. Senior, Military, 4th Grade, etc.) also known as interagency passes. For more information visit the park's Fees & Passes web page.
description.need_to_know_email:
Itineraries provided in reservations are not reviewed for compliance with conditions for the protection of wilderness . All party members are responsible for following permit conditions; violations may be cited under 36 CFR Part 2.

Your reservation is not a wilderness permit and cannot be used for overnight travel. Only the listed group leader or alternate leader identified at the time of reservation may be issued the permit. All party members should be present for an orientation on wilderness protection and safety. Bring proof of identity to pick up your wilderness permit at the designated issuing station for your entry point: 

  • Roads End Contact Station (Cedar Grove): Woods Creek, Bubbs Creek, Copper Creek, Lewis Creek, Don Cecil - East
  • Kings Canyon Visitor Center (Grant Grove): Redwood Canyon, Sugarloaf, Belle Canyon, JO Pass, Don Cecil - West
  • Lodgepole Visitor Center: High Sierra Trail, Alta, Twin Lakes, Lakes Trail, Lakes Trail Pass Through, Bearpaw High Sierra Camp, Colony Mill - East
  • Mineral King Ranger Station: Timber Gap, Sawtooth Pass, Franklin, Farewell Gap, White Chief, Eagle Lake, Mosquito Lakes, Tar Gap, Atwell-Hockett, Paradise Ridge
  • Ash Mountain Wilderness Office: Middle Fork Kaweah, Ladybug, Garfield Grove, Oriole Lake Road, North Fork Kaweah, Colony Mill - West

Permits are only issued by rangers during hours of operation . There is no night drop. Permits may be issued as early as 1:00 PM the day prior to the entry date. If you need to pick up your permit later than 10:00 AM on the entry date, notify the Wilderness Office (559-565-3766 or seki_wilderness_office@nps.gov). If you do not make arrangements for a late pickup, your reservation will be cancelled at 10:00 AM and quota made available for walk ups. 

Cancellations and changes made more than 1 week prior to the entry date may be refunded the per-person recreation fee. Changes may be made at the issuing station if quota is available; these changes will incur additional fees.

Entrance fee required.

description.need_to_know_pdf:
Wilderness protection requires your personal commitment. Plan your activities to allow time and energy for good minimum impact practices. All group members are responsible for the complying with the following minimum impact restrictions. A ranger will review these restrictions when you pick up your wilderness permit.

General Requirements

  • Carry your signed permit and present it upon request.

  • Prevent erosion and preserve vegetation, do not shortcut trails. Close fences and gates behind you.

  • Do not build cairns, walls, trenches, fire rings, or bough beds.

  • Pets are prohibited.

  • Pack out all trash including toilet paper. Caching food or equipment is prohibited.

  • Wheeled vehicles and motorized equipment are prohibited.

  • Possessing firearms is subject to state regulations; discharge is prohibited. Possession of weapons is prohibited.

  • Additional travel, party size, camping, and grazing restrictions apply to stock groups.

Party Size

  • Maximum party size is 15 people on trail, 12 people off trail, except as follows. Maximum 10 people in Redwood Canyon. Maximum 8 people on the Colony Mill Road and Don Cecil Trails, and Darwin Canyon. Maximum 8 people in the off trail areas of Dusy Basin, Sixty Lakes Basin, Sphinx Lakes, Wallace Creek, Whitney and Crabtree Creeks, Upper Rock Creek, Mt. Whitney and Mt. Langley.

  • Off trail is defined as 0.5 mi. in areas open to overnight use, 100 yds. in day use areas.

  • Affiliated groups may not travel or camp within 0.5 mi. of each other if total group size exceeds limits.

Campsites

  • Camp further than 100 ft. from water. Camping within 100 ft. of water is allowed only in established sites. Never camp within 25 ft. of water. Camp only on durable surfaces (dirt, rock, snow), never on vegetation.

  • Look up for tree hazards.

Sanitation

  • Bury human waste at least 6 inches deep and 100 ft. from trails, camps, and water. Pack out used toilet paper.

  • Carry water 100 ft. from the source to wash clothes, dishes, or yourself.

  • Poor hygiene causes illness; wash your hands often. Boil, treat, or filter drinking water.

Food Storage

  • Store food items to prevent bears or other wildlife from obtaining them. Food items include: any food for human or pack stock, toiletries, food-tainted trash, equipment with food residue.

  • Use one of three food storage methods: allowed portable animal-resistant food-storage container; animal-resistant food storage box; or counter-balance hanging technique. In areas without food storage boxes or trees for hanging, you must use an allowed portable animal-resistant food-storage container.

  • Allowed animal-resistant food-storage containers are required in the following areas May 1 through October 31: North Dome, Woods and Bubbs Creeks (including the Rae Lakes Loop), Dusy Basin, Pear and Emerald Lakes, and Rock Creek.

Campfires

  • In Kings Canyon NP fires are prohibited above 10,000 ft. and in Granite Basin and Redwood Canyon.

  • In the Kaweah and Tule River drainages of Sequoia National Park fires are prohibited above 9,000 ft and at Pinto Lake, Summit Lake, Hamilton Lakes, Dillonwood, and the Mineral King Valley. In the Kern River drainage of Sequoia NP fires are prohibited above 10,000 ft.

  • Use existing fire rings; do not add rocks.

  • Burn only dead wood from the ground. Do not burn trash, especially plastic and foil.

  • Attend fires at all times. Extinguish fires with water before leaving and stir the ashes.

Safety

  • Search and rescue is discretionary. Rescuer safety is the first priority. Exhibit self-reliance and responsibility commensurate with the riskiness of your activities.

  • If you carry a satellite device, be familiar with its operation and limitations. Do not rely on it to summon help or notify family that you are "OK." Cell phones have limited coverage, do not rely on them. If you have an emergency and cannot self-rescue, contact a ranger or Park Dispatch at (559) 565-3195. Provide clear, concise information about the nature and exact location of the emergency.

description.no_show_policy:
There is no “night drop.” All permits must be issued in person during permit issuing station hours of operation .

Your reservation will be canceled as a no show and your space may go to other groups unless you pick up your permit or arrange to hold the permit for late arrival. If you do not make arrangements for a late pickup, your reservation will be canceled at 10:00 AM on your entry date and the space released to the walk up pool. 

To arrange for pickup after 10:00 AM, contact the wilderness office at (559) 565-3766 or seki_wilderness_office@nps.gov and include "Hold request" and your reservation number in the subject line.
description.quota_details:
During the quota period (generally the Friday before Memorial Day through the Saturday that falls between September 23-29) there is a limit on the number of people each day that may enter the wilderness at a given point for overnight use. Permits are only valid for entry at a given point and date and cannot be used to enter elsewhere or on a different date.

The quota includes both private and commercially guided groups. 

A portion of the quota is available first-come, first-served for walk-ups at the permit issuing station. 

Most, but not all trailheads allow a proportion of all available entry quota to be reserved up to six months in advance. Reservations may be made up to one week prior to the entry date. Unused reservable quota space is made available for walk-ups. 

All quota season permits (reserved and walk-up) are issued in person beginning at 1:00 PM the day prior to entry. "No-shows" are made available for walk-up permits (see no-show policies under "Fees & Cancellations" tab).
description.season_information:
This reservation is for a quota season permit for overnight visitation of wilderness and backcountry areas of Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks (SEKI). Permits issued by SEKI are valid for continuous wilderness and backcountry travel in the Sequoia, Sierra, and Inyo National Forests (NF) and Yosemite National Park, subject to those agencies' conditions.

To enter SEKI from the Jennie Lake Wilderness obtain a SEKI permit for the JO Pass, Belle Canyon, or Sugarloaf entry points; to enter from the Deer Cove area of the Monarch Wilderness , obtain a SEKI permit for the Lewis Creek entry point. 

To enter SEKI from the Inyo NF , Sierra NF , Golden Trout portion of the Sequoia NF , or Yosemite NP obtain permits from those agencies; those permits are valid for continuous travel in SEKI.

Exiting wilderness overnight in SEKI ends continuous travel and invalidates the permit for further use.

Additional authorization is required to provide commercial services and for certain other activities .
description.tertiary_page:
Thoroughly review all the information on this site before making a reservation. Here are some common errors and how to avoid them.

Picking the wrong entry point

Each entry point is defined by a starting location or trailhead and a direction and minimum travel distance to the closest wilderness camp associated with that entry point. Your entry point cannot be changed after you make your reservation; it is your responsibility to review the entry point map and read the entry point descriptions (click the entry point name on the "detailed availablity" page) to select the correct entry point prior to making a reservation. Some commonly confused entry points are: 

  • Bubbs Creek/Woods Creek/Copper Creek. These all start from Roads End in Kings Canyon but require travel in different directions. Select the Woods Creek entry point to travel clockwise on the Rae Lakes Loop, and Bubbs Creek to travel counterclockwise on the Rae Lakes Loop. Copper Creek does not provide direct access to the Rae Lakes Loop.
  • High Sierra Trail/Alta. Beginning trips from Wolverton or Crescent Meadow and travelling east of the Sevenmile Hill Trail on the High Sierra trail requires a High Sierra Trail entry point on the permit. The Alta entry point cannot be used. 
  • Alta/Lakes Trail: Camping at Emerald Lake or Pear Lake the first night requires a Lakes Trail entry point which is walk-up only. 
  • Sugarloaf/Belle Canyon/JO Pass. These entry points all provide access into the parks from the Jennie Lakes Wilderness. Select Belle Canyon to travel initially to Seville, Lost, Ranger, or Beville Lakes. Select Sugarloaf to initially travel east down Sugarloaf Creek. Select JO Pass to initially travel over JO Pass into Clover Creek.
  • Paradise Ridge/Woods Creek. Paradise Ridge is near Mineral King. Select the Woods Creek entry point for access to Paradise Valley near Cedar Grove.
  • Sawtooth Pass/Timber Gap. Both start from the Sawtooth parking area but require travel in different directions. To head northward into Cliff Creek select the Timber Gap entry point. To head east to Monarch Lakes and Lost Canyon select the Sawtooth Pass entry point.
  • Franklin/Farewell Gap. The Farewell Gap entry point requires exiting Sequoia National Park at Farewell Gap and camping in the Golden Trout Wilderness prior to re-entering the park. Those wishing to travel directly to Franklin Lakes must select the Franklin entry point.

Planning an itinerary which violates camping rules

Some locations are partially or wholly closed to camping to everyone, or to camping with pack or saddle animals, or have length of stay limits due to their popularity. There is no automated check of the itinerary entered on your reservation – instead rangers at the trailhead will review the itinerary prior to issuing the permit. You are not obligated to follow the itinerary on your reservation and permit provided that you are following all the camping rules that are a condition of the permit. It is your responsibility to plan an itinerary which complies with the parks' camping restrictions. These include, but are not limited to:

  • Rae Lakes Loop: 
    • Camp only in designated sites in Lower Paradise Valley (temporarily closed). 
    • 2 night camping limit in Paradise Valley. 
    • 1 night camping limit per lake between Dollar Lake and Glen Pass. 
    • 2 night camping limit at Charlotte and Kearsarge Lakes and along the John Muir Trail from Woods Creek Crossing to Vidette Meadow.
    • No camping within 1/4 mile of Bullfrog Lake. 
  • Dusy Basin: 2 night camping limit. 
  • Muir Pass: No camping in the shelter.
  • Lakes Trail: 
    • No camping at Aster or Heather Lake. 
    • Camp only in designated sites at Pear and Emerald Lakes. 
    • 3 night limit (combined).
  • High Sierra Trail: 
    • Camp only in designated sites at Bearpaw Meadow, not at the Bearpaw High Sierra Camp or ranger station. 
    • 1 night camping limit at Hamilton Lakes.
  • Whitney/Crabtree: 
    • No camping at Timberline Lake. 
    • 2 night camping limit in the Crabtree/Whitney Creek area and Guitar Lake.
    • No camping in the Mt. Whitney shelter.
  • Rock Creek:
    • 3 night camping limit at Soldier Lakes.
  • Redwood Canyon: 2 night camping limit.
  • Don Cecil Trail: 2 night camping limit.
  • Columbine Lake: No camping.
  • Eagle & Mosquito Trails: 
    • No camping between the trail and Eagle Lake. 
    • No camping within 1/4 mile of first Mosquito Lake.
  • Hockett: No camping between the trail and Whitman Creek.

Missing your entry date

You must begin your trip on the entry date listed on your reservation; this date cannot be changed. You must pick up the permit during operating hours on your entry date or the afternoon prior to your entry date. Request a hold if you will arrive after the 10 AM "no-show" time. If you are unable to start on the day listed, you will need to obtain a new reservation or permit; if the quota is already filled you may not be able to obtain one for your planned trip. Consider travel time and early season hazards (creek crossings, snow) when selecting an entry date for your trip.

44585701.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via Lewis Creek or Hotel Creek Trails. Those starting from the Deer Cove Trail (Sequoia National Forest) and planning to travel through Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks can obtain a permit for this entry point.

Access to Grizzly Lakes, Kennedy Lakes, and Kennedy Canyon. The Lewis Creek drainage showcases recent fire ecology. The trail is hot and strenuously steep with few people. Plan to start early in the day. The trail through Kennedy Canyon is faint and should be treated as a cross-country route. 

Permits issued at Roads End Contact Station.

Parking at Lewis Creek or Hotel Creek Trailhead.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Lewis Creek entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4 miles from the Lewis Creek trailhead at Comb Creek. 

No campfires in Granite Basin or above 10,000 ft.

44585701.name: Lewis Creek

44585702.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Copper Creek Trail. 

Access to Granite Basin, Granite Lake, Volcanic Lakes, State Lakes, and Middle Fork of the Kings River. 

Hot and steep. Plan to start early in the day. 

Permits issued at Roads End Contact Station.

Parking at Roads End.

20 person daily quota; 15 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Woods Creek entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4.4 miles from Roads End at Lower Tent Meadow.

This permit does not allow you directly access the Rae Lakes Loop. To do so you must select the Woods Creek or Bubbs Creek entry point.

Use of park-allowed, portable animal-resistant food-storage containers is required May 1 - October 31 in the Bubbs and Woods Creek drainages.

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kings River drainage or in Granite Basin.

44585702.name: Copper Creek

44585703.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Woods Creek Trail. 

This is the entry point to start the popular Rae Lakes Loop in the easier clockwise direction. Provides access to the John Muir and Pacific Crest Trails at Woods Creek Crossing. A popular trail with many people at any given time. 

Permits issued at Roads End Contact Station.

Parking at Roads End.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Woods Creek entry point:

The first allowable camping is 6.5 miles from Roads End at Lower Paradise Valley.

This permit does not allow you to start the Rae Lakes loop in the counter-clockwise direction. To do so you must select the Bubbs Creek entry point.

Use of park-allowed, portable animal-resistant food-storage containers is required May 1 - October 31 in the Bubbs and Woods Creek drainages.

Use designated sites only in Lower Paradise Valley. No camping within 0.25 miles of Bullfrog Lake.

Two night camping limit for Paradise Valley, Charlotte Lake, Kearsarge Lakes, and one night camping limit per lake in the Rae Lakes area (from Dollar Lake to Glen Pass).

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kings River drainage.

44585703.name: Woods Creek

44585704.description:
Provides entry into wilderness via Bubbs Creek. 

This is the entry point to start the popular Rae Lakes Loop in the more strenuous counter-clockwise direction. Provides access to East Lake and the John Muir and Pacific Crest Trails at Vidette Meadow. Popular trail with many people at any given time. Dramatic and diverse. Steep and strenuous to Sphinx Creek, then steady and moderate climb. 

Permits issued at Roads End Contact Station.

Parking at Roads End.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Bubbs Creek entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4 miles from Roads End at Sphinx Creek crossing. 

This permit does not allow you to start the Rae Lakes loop in the clockwise direction. To do so you must select the Woods Creek entry point.

Use of park-allowed, portable animal-resistant food-storage containers is required May 1 - October 31 in the Bubbs and Woods Creek drainages.

Use designated sites only in Lower Paradise Valley. No camping within 0.25 miles of Bullfrog Lake.

Two night camping limit for Paradise Valley, Charlotte Lake, Kearsarge Lakes, and one night camping limit per lake in the Rae Lakes area (from Dollar Lake to Glen Pass).

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kings River drainage.

44585704.name: Bubbs Creek

44585705.description:
** Closed due to fire until further notice **

Entry into wilderness via Redwood Saddle Trailhead, including the Redwood Canyon, Hart Tree, and Sugar Bowl Trails. 

Relatively easy trail through one of the largest sequoia groves. Two 6.5-mile loops can be combined. 

Permits issued at Kings Canyon Visitor Center.

Parking at Redwood Saddle. The dirt/gravel Redwood Saddle Road may be impassible in the early season.

15 person daily quota; 10 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Redwood Canyon entry point:

First allowable camping is 1 mile from Redwood Saddle at Redwood Creek. 

Maximum group size is 10 people.

Two-night camping limit.

No campfires allowed.

No overnight stock use.

44585705.name: Redwood Canyon

44585706.description:
Provides entry into Kings Canyon National Park from the Jennie Lakes Wilderness (Sequoia National Forest) via the Kanawyer Gap or Sugarloaf/Pond Meadow entrances. Access is from the Big Meadows Road. To spend the first night in the parks at Seville Lake, Lost Lake, or Ranger Lake, select the "Belle Canyon" entrance point.

Moderately strenuous. Forests, creeks, meadows, glaciated canyons. Good area for stock travel. Combine with the JO Pass Trail for a loop option through Jennie Lakes Wilderness.

Permits issued at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center.

25 person daily quota; 15 reservable.

No wilderness permit is required for camping only in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness . For more information call the Hume Lake Ranger District at (559) 338-2251.

description_map.need_to_know:
Sugarloaf entry point:

This entry point does not camping the first night in the parks at Seville Lake, Lost Lake, or Ranger Lake; to do so select the Belle Canyon entrance point.

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in Kings Canyon.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage of Sequoia National Park.

Travelers may camp in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness before reaching the parks boundary.

44585706.name: Sugarloaf

44585707.description:
Entry into Kings Canyon National Park from the Jennie Lakes Wilderness (Sequoia National Forest) via the Belle Canyon entrance to Seville Lake, Lost Lake, and Ranger Lakes.  Access from the Big Meadows Road. 

Moderately strenuous. Forests, creeks, meadows, glaciated canyons. Good area for stock travel. Combine with the JO Pass Trail for a loop option through Jennie Lakes Wilderness. 

Permits issued at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center.

25 person daily quota; 15 reservable.

No wilderness permit is required for camping only in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness in the Hume Lake Ranger District.

description_map.need_to_know:
Belle Canyon entry point:

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in Kings Canyon. No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage of Sequoia National Park.

Travelers may camp in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness before reaching the parks boundary.

44585707.name: Belle Canyon

44585708.description:
** This entry point accesses an area burned in 2021 and may contain hazards associated with the fire **

Entry into Sequoia National Park from the Jennie Lakes Wilderness (Sequoia National Forest) via the JO Pass entrance. Access from the Big Meadows Road or Stony Creek. To travel directly to Seville Lake, Lost Lake, or Ranger Lake, select the "Belle Canyon" entrance point.

Moderately strenuous. Forests, creeks, meadows, glaciated canyons. Combine with the Belle Canyon or Sugarloaf trails for a loop trip through the Jennie Lakes Wilderness.

Permits issued at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center.

15 person daily quota; 10 reservable.

No wilderness permit is required for camping only in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness in the Hume Lake Ranger District.

description_map.need_to_know:
JO Pass entry point:

No campfires above 10,000 ft. in Kings Canyon. No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage of Sequoia National Park.

Travelers may camp in the Jennie Lakes Wilderness before reaching the parks boundary.

44585708.name: JO Pass

44585709.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via Wolverton Trailhead and the Lakes Trail to Pear and Emerald Lakes. Daily entry is limited by destination quotas for each lake basin.

Moderately strenuous. Forests and glacier carved subalpine lake basins. The Watchtower Trail is not recommended when snowy, wet, or icy conditions exist. This is a popular area with high overnight and day use visitation. 

Permits issued at the Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Parking at Wolverton.

Up to 25 person daily quota limited by occupancy at Pear and Emerald Lake basins with a maximum occupancy of 15 persons at either lake; no reservations are available.

description_map.need_to_know:
Lakes Trail entry point (destination quota):

First allowable camping is 5 miles from Wolverton at Emerald Lake. 

Camping is allowed only in designated sites at Pear and Emerald Lake. No camping at Heather or Aster Lakes or in the Marble Fork drainage below Emerald and Pear Lakes. Camping is limited to 3 nights total between Pear and Emerald Lakes.

Use of park-allowed, portable animal-resistant food-storage containers is required May 1 - October 31 at Pear and Emerald Lakes

No campfires are allowed (area is above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage).

Outhouses have been provided at Pear and Emerald Lakes due to the lack of soil. Only human waste, no trash, should be placed in the outhouses.

No overnight stock use.

44585709.name: Lakes Trail

44585710.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Alta Peak Trail which dead-ends at Alta Meadow and Alta Peak. 

This entry point does not allow travel on the High Sierra Trail between the Sevenmile Hill Trail and Kaweah Gap; to do so select a "High Sierra Trail" entry point instead.

Forests, expansive views. Steady climb to Alta Peak (11,291 ft). No water at Panther Gap. 

Permits issued at the Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Parking at Wolverton.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Alta entry point:

First allowable camping is 3 miles from Wolverton at Panther Gap. No camping at Pear or Emerald Lakes on first night of trip.

This permit does not allow travel on the High Sierra Trail between the Sevenmile Hill Trail and Kaweah Gap.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage (allowed at Panther Gap and Mehrten Meadow).

No overnight stock use.

44585710.name: Alta

44585711.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the High Sierra Trail starting from either Crescent Meadow or Wolverton. 

The High Sierra Trail is a dramatic trans-Sierra route that crosses the Great Western Divide, drops to the Kern Canyon, and ultimately leads to Mount Whitney. Due its popularity, expect to see many people.

Permits issued at the Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Parking available at Crescent Meadow or Wolverton.

30 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

Bearpaw High Sierra Camp guests are exempt from entry quota and fee if staying overnight at the camp only; obtain a walk-up permit. The quota and fees apply if camping elsewhere.

description_map.need_to_know:
High Sierra Trail entry point:

First allowable camping is 2.8 mi. from Crescent Meadow at Panther Creek or 3 mi. from Wolverton at Panther Gap. 

Camp only at designated sites at Bearpaw Meadow. One night camping limit at Hamilton Lakes. Two night camping limit in the Whitney Creek drainage. No camping at Timberline Lake.  

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage. No fires at Hamilton Lakes or Pinto Lakes. No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kern River drainage. 

Travellers to the upper Whitney Creek drainage (Guitar Lake, Mount Whitney) should obtain and use a carry out waste kit to minimize human waste impacts in this very popular area.

No stock travel on High Sierra Trail between Crescent Meadow and Wolverton Cutoff Trail.

44585711.name: High Sierra Trail

44585712.description:
** This entry point accesses an area burned in 2021 and may contain hazards associated with the fire **

Provides entry into the wilderness via the Middle Fork Kaweah or Paradise Creek Trails.

Access to Redwood Meadow, Cliff Creek, High Sierra Trail. Slight grade along Middle Fork of Kaweah River and then steepens after 13 miles. Oaks, chaparral, river, vistas. Best in spring, fall, and winter; not recommended in heat of summer. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes.

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Park at the Middle Fork Kaweah Trailhead (no parking at Buckeye Campground). The Middle Fork Road may be closed due to wet conditions; park at Hospital Rock Picnic Area instead.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Middle Fork Kaweah entry point:

The first allowable camping area is 3.5 miles from Middle Fork Trailhead at Panther Creek, or 2 miles from the Middle Fork Bridge at Poison Oak Flat. 

Camp only at designated sites at Bearpaw Meadow. One night camping limit at Hamilton Lakes.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage. No fires at Hamilton Lakes or Pinto Lakes.

44585712.name: Middle Fork Kaweah

44585713.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Ladybug Trail. 

Short trail ends at South Fork Grove in 5 miles. First camping area 1.7 miles to Ladybug Camp. Relatively easy, short trail ends at the South Fork Grove of giant sequoia in 5 miles. Giant sequoia trees, river. Best in spring, fall, and winter. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes.

This area burned in the 2020 SQF Complex Fire. Be aware of hazards such as falling trees and rocks and unstable slopes.

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Parking at the South Fork Trailhead (no parking in the South Fork Campground).

15 person daily quota; 10 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Ladybug entry point:

The first allowable camping is 1.7 miles from South Fork Campground at Ladybug Camp. 

No fires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage.

No overnight stock use.

44585713.name: Ladybug

44585714.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Garfield Grove Trail. 

Access to the Hockett Plateau. Steep and challenging climb. Good early-season trail. Giant sequoia trees; meadows and lakes on plateau. Good area for stock travel. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes at lower elevations.

This area burned in the 2020 SQF Complex Fire. Be aware of hazards such as falling trees and rocks and unstable slopes.

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Parking at the South Fork Trailhead (no parking at the South Fork Campground).

15 person daily quota; 10 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Garfield Grove entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4 miles from the South Fork Campground at Snowslide Canyon. 

No campfires above 9,000 ft in the Kaweah River and Tule River drainages. No fires at Summit Lake.

44585714.name: Garfield Grove

44585715.description:
** This entry point accesses an area burned in 2021 and may contain hazards associated with the fire **

Provides entry into wilderness via the Paradise Ridge Trail. 

Access to Redwood Meadow and Cliff Creek. Steep and dry on both sides of Paradise Ridge. Giant Sequoias and vistas. Trail may be difficult to follow.  

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the Atwell Mill Trailhead.

15 person daily quota; 10 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Paradise Ridge entry point:

The first allowable camping is 3.3 miles from Atwell Mill Campground at Paradise Ridge (no water). 

This trail does not directly access Paradise Valley in Kings Canyon and is not a starting point for the Rae Lakes Loop.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage or at Pinto Lake or Hamilton Lakes.

44585715.name: Paradise Ridge

44585716.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Timber Gap Trail. 

Access to Cliff Creek. Moderately strenuous. Forests, subalpine. Combine with Sawtooth Pass, or Franklin Pass trails for loop options through the Little and Big Five Lakes Basins. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the Sawtooth Trailhead.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Timber Gap entry point:

The first allowable camping is 2.3 miles from the Sawtooth Trailhead at Timber Gap (no water). 

This permit does not allow travel directly eastward to Monarch or Crystal Lakes. To do so you must select the Sawtooth Pass entry point.

No camping at Columbine Lake or Little Claire Lake. 1 night camping limit at Hamilton Lake.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage or at Pinto Lake or Hamilton Lakes or in Mineral King Valley above the ranger station. No fires above 10,000 ft. in the Kern River drainage.

44585716.name: Timber Gap

44585717.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Monarch Lakes Trail. 

Access to Kern Canyon. Can combine Timber Gap or Franklin Pass exit points for loop options. Steep and strenuous. Lakes, vistas. The trail between Monarch Lakes and Columbine Lake over Sawtooth Pass is rough and difficult to follow.  

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at Sawtooth Trailhead.

20 person daily quota; 15 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Sawtooth Pass entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4.2 miles from the Sawtooth Trailhead at Lower Monarch Lake or 4.9 miles from the Sawtooth Trailhead at Crystal Lake. 

This permit does not allow travel directly northward to Cliff Creek. To do so you must select the Timber Gap entry point.

No camping at Columbine Lake or Little Claire Lake. 1 night camping limit at Hamilton Lake.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage or at Pinto Lake or Hamilton Lakes or in Mineral King Valley above the ranger station. No fires above 10,000 ft. in the Kern River drainage.

No stock travel allowed.

44585717.name: Sawtooth Pass

44585718.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Atwell-Hockett Trail.

Access to the Hockett Plateau. Moderately strenuous. Giant Sequoias, forests, meadows. Good area for stock travel. 9.8 miles to Hockett Meadow. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the Atwell Mill Trailhead.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Atwell-Hockett entry point:

The first allowable camping is 6 miles from Atwell Mill Campground at Clover Creek. 

No camping between trail and Whitman Creek at Hockett Meadow. 

No campfires above 9,000 ft in the Kaweah River and Tule River drainages. No fires at Summit Lake.

44585718.name: Atwell-Hockett

44585719.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Tar Gap Trail. 

Access to the Hockett Plateau. Moderately strenuous. Giant Sequoias, forests, meadows. Good area for stock travel. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking 0.3 mi. east of Mineral King Ranger Station (no parking in Cold Springs Campground).

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Tar Gap entry point:

The first allowable camping is 6 miles from Cold Springs Campground at Deer Creek. 

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah and Tule River drainages. No campfires in the Mineral King Valley above the Mineral King Ranger Station. No campfires at Summit Lake.

44585719.name: Tar Gap

44585720.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Mosquito Lakes Trail. 

Moderately strenuous. Lakes, forests, vistas. Cross-country travel is required to reach the allowed camping areas in the upper Mosquito Lakes and Mineral Lakes basins. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the end of the road in the upper Mineral King Valley.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Mosquito Lakes entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4.1 miles from the trailhead at Mosquito Lake #2. No camping at lowest Mosquito Lake. 

This permit does not allow you to spend your first night at White Chief or Eagle Lake. To do so you must select one of those entry points.

No campfires. 

Overnight stock use only for walking parties with burros or llamas.

44585720.name: Mosquito Lakes

44585721.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Eagle Lake Trail. 

Moderately strenuous. Lakes, forests, vistas.  

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the end of the road in the upper Mineral King Valley.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Eagle Lake entry point:

The first allowable camping is 3.4 miles from the trailhead at Eagle Lake. 

If your first night is at White Chief or Mosquito Lakes you must select one of those entry points.

No camping between the trail and Eagle Lake. 

No campfires. 

Overnight stock use only for walking parties with burros or llamas.

44585721.name: Eagle Lake

44585722.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the White Chief Trail. 

Moderately strenuous. Colorful canyon filled with history. Meadows, sinkholes, vistas. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the end of the road in the upper Mineral King Valley.

25 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
White Chief entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4.1 miles from the trailhead in the White Chief valley. 

This permit does not allow you to spend your first night at Eagle Lake or Mosquito Lakes. To do so you must select one of those entry points.

No campfires. 

Overnight stock use only for walking parties with burros or llamas.

44585722.name: White Chief

44585723.description:
Provides entry into the Golden Trout Wilderness (Sequoia National Forest) via the Farewell Gap Trail. 

Access to Little Kern River and Kern Canyon. Steep and strenuous. Trails in the Golden Trout Wilderness may be difficult to follow due to brush and downed tress. Lakes, vistas. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the end of the road in the upper Mineral King Valley or at Sawtooth Trailhead.

30 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Farewell Gap entry point:

No camping at Franklin Lakes without exiting the park and remaining overnight in the Sequoia National Forest. To access Franklin Lakes directly select the Franklin entry point.

No camping at Columbine Lake.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage or at Pinto Lake or Hamilton Lakes or in Mineral King Valley above the ranger station. No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kern River Drainage.

44585723.name: Farewell Gap

44585724.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Franklin Pass Trail. 

Access to Rattlesnake Creek and Kern Canyon. Steep and strenuous. Lakes, vistas. Combine with Timber Gap, Sawtooth Pass or Farewell Gap trails for loop options. 

Permits issued at the Mineral King Ranger Station.

Parking at the end of the road in the upper Mineral King Valley or at Sawtooth Trailhead.

30 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Franklin entry point:

The first allowable camping is 4 miles from the trailhead at the Franklin-Farewell Trail Junction. 

No camping at Columbine Lake. 1 night camping limit at Hamilton Lake.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage or at Pinto Lake or Hamilton Lakes or in Mineral King Valley above the ranger station. No campfires above 10,000 ft. in the Kern River Drainage.

44585724.name: Franklin

44585725.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness via the Lakes Trail and cross-country travel. No camping at Pear and Emerald Lakes is allowed under this entry point.

Provides access via cross-country travel to Moose Lake and the Tablelands. Accessing allowed camping areas requires cross country travel from Pear Lake. Moderately strenuous. Watchtower Trail not recommended when snowy, wet, or icy conditions exist. Forests and glacier carved subalpine lake basins. High visitation in areas accessed by trails. 

Permits issued at Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Parking at Wolverton.

25 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Lakes Trail Pass Through entry point:

The first allowable camping is approximately 7 miles from Wolverton (and 0.5 mi east of Pear Lake) in the upper Marble Fork Kaweah drainage. Cross country travel is required to reach allowed camping. No camping is allowed at Pear or Emerald Lake under this entry point.

No camping at Heather or Aster Lakes or in the Marble Fork drainage below Emerald and Pear Lakes. 

No campfires are allowed (area is above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage). 

Outhouses have been provided at Pear and Emerald Lakes due to the lack of soil. Only human waste, no trash, should be placed in the outhouses.

No overnight stock use.

44585725.name: Lakes Trail Pass Through

44585726.description:
** Closed due to fire until further notice **

Provides entry into the wilderness from the east end of the Colony Mill Trail. 

Historic access road to Sequoia National Park. Forests. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes at lower elevations. Water may not be available along trail. Best in spring, fall, and winter. 

Permits issued at Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Limited parking at trailhead on the Crystal Cave Road. 

8 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Colony Mill East entry point:

The first allowable camping is 2.5 miles west of the Crystal Cave Road. 

Two night camping limit.

Maximum group size 8 people.

44585726.name: Colony Mill East

44585727.description:
** Closed due to fire until further notice **

Provides entry into the wilderness from the west end of the Colony Mill Trail. 

Historic access road to Sequoia National Park. Forests. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes at lower elevations. Water may not be available along trail. Best in spring, fall, and winter; not recommended in heat of summer. 

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Parking at the end of North Fork Road at Yucca Creek.

8 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Colony Mill West entry point:

The first allowable camping is 2 miles east of the trailhead at Maple Creek. 

Two night camping limit.

Maximum group size 8 people.

44585727.name: Colony Mill West

44585728.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness from the east end of the Don Cecil Trail in Cedar Grove. 

Historic access trail to Cedar Grove. Forests. Hot, strenuously steep, few people. Plan to start early in the day. 

Permits issued at Roads End Contact Station.

Parking in turnout along the road or at entrance to Sentinel Campground.

8 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Don Cecil East entry point:

The first allowable camping is 2 miles west of trailhead. 

Two night camping limit.

Maximum group size 8 people.

44585728.name: Don Cecil East

44585729.description:
Provides entry into the wilderness from the west end of the Don Cecil Trail in the Sequoia National Forest at the end of the Big Meadows Road near Summit Meadow and Lookout Peak. 

Historic access trail to Cedar Grove. Forests. Hot, strenuously steep, few people. Plan to start early in the day. 

Permits issued at the Kings Canyon Visitor Center.

Parking along Big Meadows Road (Forest Route 14S11).

description_map.need_to_know:
Don Cecil West entry point:

The first allowable camping is 1 miles east of Summit Meadow. 

Two night camping limit.

Maximum group size 8 people.

44585729.name: Don Cecil West

44585730.description:
** This entry point accesses an area burned in 2021 and may contain hazards associated with the fire **

Provides entry into the wilderness via the North Fork Kaweah Trail. 

Moderately strenuous. Oaks, chaparral, river, vistas. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes. Best in spring, fall, and winter; not recommended in heat of summer. The trail becomes difficult to follow past Burnt Point Creek and should be treated as a cross country route. 

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Parking at the end of North Fork Drive at Yucca Creek.

15 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
North Fork Kaweah entry point:

The first allowable camping 1 mile from trailhead (no water). 

No camping in Muir Grove.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage.

44585730.name: North Fork Kaweah

44585731.description:
** Closed due to fire until further notice **

Entry into the wilderness via the Oriole Lake Road and cross-country travel. The Milk Ranch Peak and Oriole Lake Roads are the only maintained travel ways; there are no maintained trails.

Oaks, chaparral, river, vistas. Best in spring, fall, and winter. Watch for ticks, poison oak, and rattlesnakes. 

Permits issued at the Ash Mountain Wilderness Office.

Limited roadside parking near the boundary gate; do not block road.

8 person daily quota; 0 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Oriole Lake entry point:

First allowable camping 1 mile from all roads at the Oriole Grove. Cross country travel is required to reach allowed camping areas.

Maximum group size 8 people.

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage.

No camping within 1 mile of any road. No trespassing on private inholdings.

No overnight stock use.

44585731.name: Oriole Lake

44585732.description:
** This entry point accesses an area burned in 2021 and may contain hazards associated with the fire **

Provides entry into the wilderness via the Twin Lakes Trail beginning at the Lodgepole Campground or from Wuksachi.

Moderately strenuous. Forests, meadows, lakes. Connect with Belle Canyon and JO Pass Trail to make a lollipop loop.

Permits issued at the Lodgepole Visitor Center.

Parking at Lodgepole near the Walter Fry Nature Center or at the lot northeast of Wuksachi Lodge.

30 person daily quota; 20 reservable.

description_map.need_to_know:
Twin Lakes entry point:

First allowable camping is 3 miles from Lodgepole or Wuksachi at Cahoon Meadow. 

No campfires above 9,000 ft. in the Kaweah River drainage of Sequoia National Park (includes Twin Lakes). No campfires above 10,000 ft. in Kings Canyon.

44585732.name: Twin Lakes

entrances.name: John Muir Trail North of Devils Postpile
John Muir Trail South of Devils Postpile
North Fork of Lone Pine Creek

Reservations for the 2026 quota season available in a rolling window (6 months to 1 week before entry date).
2026 quota season. Daily entry limited by number of people and entry point. Recreation fee required.
Non-quota period. Self-issue wilderness permits available at visitors centers and not subject to daily entry limits or fee.

payload.in_station_info:
All the advanced permits for this trailhead on this date have been taken. All that remain are the first come, first served, Walkup permits, which become available, in person at 1:00 PM the day prior to the trip date and remain available during operating hours until closing time the date of the trip. 

You may also continue to check back for cancelations, which can occur at anytime, up until a week before the trip date.
